ai.literal: Without moving far away, without approaching too close, like those who warm themselves by fire, let those who associate with and conduct themselves before mighty kings be.
ai.translation: Let those who associate with mighty kings conduct themselves like people warming themselves by a fire—neither staying too far away, nor drawing too close.
ai.modern: வலிமைமிக்க அரசர்களுடன் பழகி வாழ்பவர்கள், நெருப்பில் குளிர் காய்வோரைப் போல, மிகத் தூரத்திலும் விலகாமல், மிக அருகிலும் நெருங்காமல் பக்குவமாக நடந்து கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises ministers and courtiers on how to maintain a safe and respectful relationship with powerful rulers. It uses the vivid analogy of warming oneself by a fire. If you stand too far away, you do not receive its warmth; if you get too close, you get burned. Similarly, being too distant from a king leads to neglect, while being too familiar or close can provoke anger and ruin. The word 'ikal' here highlights the formidable power of the king, which must be treated with constant caution.

ai.literal: Not desiring the things that kings desire will give enduring wealth by those kings.
ai.translation: Abstaining from desiring the very things that rulers desire for themselves will bring enduring prosperity through those same rulers.
ai.modern: அரசர்கள் விரும்பும் பொருள்களைத் தான் விரும்பாமல் இருப்பது, அந்த அரசர்களாலேயே ஒருவருக்கு நிலைத்த செல்வத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises courtiers and associates on how to behave safely and successfully around rulers. The word 'viḻaipa' refers to the specific objects, pleasures, or privileges that a king desires or enjoys. By practicing 'viḻaiyāmai' (not desiring those same things), an associate avoids provoking the ruler's jealousy, suspicion, or rivalry. This self-restraint wins the ruler's trust, which ultimately yields 'manniya ākkam' (enduring wealth and position) bestowed by the ruler himself.

ai.literal: If [one wants to] protect [oneself], protecting [against] difficult things [is necessary]; after [the ruler] suspects, reassuring [him] is difficult for anyone.
ai.translation: If you wish to protect yourself, guard against committing grave errors or revealing secrets; once suspicion is aroused in the ruler's mind, it is impossible for anyone to reassure him.
ai.modern: தன்னைத் தற்காத்துக் கொள்ள விரும்பினால், அரிய தவறுகள் நேராதவாறு (அல்லது இரகசியங்களை) காக்க வேண்டும்; அரசர் சந்தேகம் கொண்ட பிறகு, அவரது ஐயத்தைப் போக்கித் தெளிவிப்பது எவருக்கும் இயலாத காரியம் ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises those who associate closely with rulers on how to maintain their safety. The poet emphasizes that the most crucial defense is to avoid committing serious mistakes or leaking confidential matters ('அரியவை போற்றல்'). Once a ruler begins to harbor suspicion ('கடுத்தபின்'), it becomes nearly impossible for anyone—including the accused or their allies—to clear that doubt and restore trust ('தேற்றுதல் யார்க்கும் அரிது'). Therefore, prevention through careful conduct is the only reliable safeguard.

ai.literal: Whispering in the ear and shared laughter, having suppressed, behaving, in the presence of abundant great people.
ai.translation: In the presence of great rulers, one must conduct oneself by avoiding whispering in another's ear and sharing private smiles.
ai.modern: அறிவு ஒழுக்கங்களில் சிறந்த பெரியவர்களின் முன்னிலையில், மற்றொருவர் காதில் இரகசியம் பேசுவதையும், அவருடன் சேர்ந்து சிரிப்பதையும் தவிர்த்து நடக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the essential etiquette to be observed when in the presence of rulers or highly placed individuals. Whispering into another person's ear and sharing private smiles or laughter are actions that can breed suspicion, appearing as if one is gossiping or mocking the ruler. To prevent such misunderstandings, a subordinate must completely suppress these habits. Conducting oneself with such restraint in their presence preserves dignity and fosters mutual trust.

ai.literal: Any matter whatsoever they will not pry into, they will not pursue; but when that matter is disclosed, let them listen to the secret.
ai.translation: Those who associate with rulers should never pry into any of their affairs, nor pursue them with questions; but when the ruler himself chooses to disclose a secret, they may listen to it.
ai.modern: அரசரோடு பழகுகின்றவர்கள் எந்த ஒரு விஷயத்தையும் ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்க மாட்டார்கள்; அதனைத் தொடர்ந்து கேட்கவும் மாட்டார்கள். ஆனால், அரசர் அந்த ரகசியத்தை அவராகவே வெளியிடும்போது மட்டும் அதனைக் கேட்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises courtiers on how to handle confidential matters in the presence of a ruler. A wise associate does not pry into the ruler's affairs or ask probing questions to uncover secrets. They must show restraint and not pursue matters that are not voluntarily shared. However, if the ruler chooses to disclose a secret on their own accord, the associate may then listen to it. The key words 'ஓரார்' (will not pry) and 'தொடரார்' (will not pursue) emphasize the strict boundaries of curiosity one must maintain around authority.

ai.literal: Knowing the intention, considering the time, speaking things that are desired, which are free from dislike, in a manner that pleases.
ai.translation: Understanding the ruler's mind and choosing the right moment, one should speak what is necessary in an agreeable manner, avoiding anything that causes dislike.
ai.modern: அரசனின் குறிப்பை அறிந்து, ஏற்ற காலத்தை ஆராய்ந்து, அவனுக்கு வெறுப்பு தராதவற்றை, அவன் விரும்பும் வண்ணம் அவன் விரும்பும் காரியங்களைச் சொல்ல வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the art of communicating with a ruler or superior. First, the speaker must read the ruler's unspoken thoughts or mood (kuṟippu). Second, they must wait for the opportune moment (kālam). Third, the message must be delivered without causing any annoyance or dislike (veṟuppila). Finally, the speaker should present the necessary matters (vēṇṭupa) in a pleasing, acceptable manner (vēṭpa).

ai.literal: Pleasing things speaking, useless things at all times, even if asked, not speaking, refrain.
ai.translation: Speak only of things that are pleasing to the ruler; even if asked, always refrain from speaking about things that are unproductive or harmful.
ai.modern: அரசருக்குப் பிடிக்கும் காரியங்களை மட்டும் பேசி, அவரே கேட்டாலும் பயனில்லாத காரியங்களை எக்காலத்திலும் சொல்லாமல் தவிர்த்துவிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet guides those who serve or advise rulers on the art of safe and effective communication. A courtier should proactively speak of matters that are agreeable and beneficial (வேட்பன சொல்லி). Conversely, matters that are useless, harmful, or lack constructive action (வினையில) must never be spoken of, even if the ruler specifically inquires about them (கேட்பினும் சொல்லா விடல்). This selective silence protects the advisor and maintains the harmony of the court.

ai.literal: Thinking 'they are younger' or 'they are related as kin', without disrespecting, it is fit to behave in accordance with the abiding majesty.
ai.translation: One should not disrespect a ruler thinking, 'He is younger than me,' or 'He is my relative'; rather, one must conduct oneself in accordance with the majestic authority they possess.
ai.modern: அரசர் நமக்கு வயதில் இளையவர் என்றும், நமக்கு உறவினர் என்றும் எண்ணி அவரை மதிக்காமல் இருக்கக் கூடாது; அவருடைய அரச பதவியின் பெருமையைப் போற்றி அதற்கேற்ப நடந்து கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises those who associate with rulers or leaders on how to maintain proper respect. Even if a ruler is younger in age or a close relative, one must not treat them with familiarity or contempt. Instead, one must recognize and respect the sovereign authority and dignity, represented here by 'ஒளி' (majesty or light), that their position holds, and behave accordingly.

ai.literal: "We are highly accepted," thinking thus, unacceptable deeds they will not do, those of unwavering clear understanding.
ai.translation: Those of unwavering, clear wisdom will not perform unacceptable deeds, presuming, "We have been highly favored and accepted by the ruler."
ai.modern: "நாம் அரசரால் ஏற்றுக்கொள்ளப்பட்டுவிட்டோம்" என்று எண்ணிக் கொண்டு, செய்யத்தகாத செயல்களைத் தெளிவான அறிவுடையவர்கள் செய்யமாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises ministers and courtiers on how to behave when they enjoy the ruler's favor. People of unwavering clarity and wisdom ('துளக்கற்ற காட்சியவர்') never let their privileged position get to their heads. They do not presume upon their closeness to the ruler ('கொளப்பட்டேம் என்று எண்ணி') to commit improper or forbidden acts ('கொள்ளாத செய்யார்'). Their steady intellect keeps them mindful that royal favor is no license for transgression.

ai.literal: Thinking 'we are old friends' and doing things that are not courteous, that over-familiarity will bring ruin.
ai.translation: The over-familiarity that leads one to behave discourteously, presuming on long-standing friendship, will bring about one's ruin.
ai.modern: "நாங்கள் பழைய நண்பர்கள்" என்று நினைத்துக்கொண்டு, தகுதியற்ற செயல்களைச் செய்யத் தூண்டும் அளவுக்கு மீறிய உரிமை பாராட்டுதல் அழிவைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against taking relationships with rulers or superiors for granted. A person might assume that their long-standing friendship (pazhaiyam) allows them to bypass etiquette. However, behaving discourteously (paṇpu alla seyyum) out of such over-familiarity (kezhuthakaimai) will ultimately lead to their downfall and ruin (kēḍu tharum).
